title: Characterization of the iridocorneal angle in humans in vivo using OCT gonioscopy.
summary: The intraocular pressure (IOP) is the only modifiable risk factor in the progression of glaucoma, a group of eye conditions that can lead to vision loss by damaging the optic nerve, usually due to high eye pressure. Many treatments aim to target the trabecular meshwork (TM), a crucial component in the eye's drainage system that helps control the flow of aqueous humor out of the eye, thereby regulating IOP. However, visualizing this area in vivo presents challenges due to optical limitations encountered when imaging through the cornea at high angles. Optical coherence tomography (OCT), a non-invasive imaging technique that provides high-resolution images of the eye's internal structures, offers a potential solution to these challenges. Our goal is to utilize OCT technology to examine the TM, Schlemm's canal (SC), and adjacent structures in the iridocorneal angle (ICA) for better understanding and treatment options. We plan to conduct OCT imaging on 100 healthy subjects and 100 glaucoma patients using three standard OCT devices. We will evaluate OCT volume scans of the TM based on their image quality, ability to visualize the SC and identify any narrowing in cases of glaucoma, and to compare the ICA. The use of OCT could allow for a more detailed characterization of the TM and SC in vivo, enabling the identification of differences in these structures associated with various pathologies.
